subject: Agriculture
title: Cover Crops
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Cover Crops.

hook.text: After harvest, most fields sit bare for months. Bare soil erodes, loses nutrients, and grows weeds.

buildup.text: Cover crops—planted not for harvest but for soil protection—keep the ground covered between cash crops.

discovery.text: Legume covers fix nitrogen. Grass covers prevent erosion. Radishes break up compacted layers with deep roots.

twist.text: Cover crops cost money to plant and produce no direct income. Many farmers see them as an expense.

climax.text: Long-term studies show cover crops pay back through better yields, less erosion, and lower fertilizer needs.

punchline.text: The crop you don't sell may be the most valuable one you grow.

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of cover crops?
options: To protect and improve soil between cash crop seasons
